# 2 Samuel Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 182r–183r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_013_page_001.jpg, 2SA_013_page_002.jpg, 2SA_013_page_003.jpg

---

**13:1** And-it-was after thus: and-to-Avshalom son of-David [was] a-sister beautiful, and-her-name [was] Tamar, and-loved-her Amnon son of-David.

**13:2** And-it-was-distressing [vayetser] to-Amnon to-the-point-of-making-himself-sick [lehitchalot] on-account-of Tamar his-sister, for a-virgin [betulah] [was]-she, and-it-was-difficult [yippale] in-[the]-eyes of-Amnon to-do to-her anything.

**13:3** And-to-Amnon [was] a-friend [re'a], and-his-name [was] Yonadav son of-Shim'ah, brother of-David; and-Yonadav [was] a-man very wise [chakham].

**13:4** And-he-said to-him, "Why [are]-you thus thin [dal], son of-the-king, morning by-morning? Will-you-not tell me?" And-said to-him Amnon, "Tamar, sister of-Avshalom my-brother, I [am]-loving."

**13:5** And-said to-him Yonadav, "Lie-down upon your-bed and-make-yourself-sick [hitchal], and-comes your-father to-see-you, and-you-shall-say to-him, 'Let-come, please, Tamar my-sister and-let-her-feed-me [literally: give-me-bread-of-sickness] food [biryah], and-let-her-make the-food before-my-eyes so-that I-may-see, and-I-will-eat from-her-hand.'"

**13:6** And-lay-down Amnon and-made-himself-sick, and-came the-king to-see-him, and-said Amnon to the-king, "Let-come, please, Tamar my-sister and-let-her-make before-my-eyes two heart-shaped-cakes [levivot], and-let-me-eat-food-of-the-sick from-her-hand."

**13:7** And-sent David to Tamar to-the-house, saying, "Go, please, to-[the]-house of-Amnon your-brother and-make for-him the-food [biryah]."

**13:8** And-went Tamar to-[the]-house of-Amnon her-brother, and-he [was]-lying-down. And-she-took the-dough and-kneaded and-made-heart-shaped-cakes [vattelabbev] before-his-eyes and-cooked the-heart-shaped-cakes [levivot].

**13:9** And-she-took the-pan [masret] and-poured-out before-him, and-he-refused to-eat. And-said Amnon, "Send-out every man from-upon-me." And-went-out every man from-upon-him.

**13:10** And-said Amnon to Tamar, "Bring the-food to-the-inner-room [cheder] and-I-will-eat from-your-hand." And-took Tamar the-heart-shaped-cakes that she-had-made and-brought [them] to-Amnon her-brother to-the-inner-room.

**13:11** And-she-brought-near to-him to-eat, and-he-seized-her [vayachazek-bah] and-said to-her, "Come, lie with-me, my-sister."

**13:12** And-she-said to-him, "No, my-brother, do-not-force-me [al-te'anneniy], for not is-done thus in-Yisra'el. Do-not do this disgraceful-thing [nevalah].

**13:13** And-I — where would-I-carry my-shame [cherpah]? And-you — you-will-be as-one of-the-disgraceful-ones [nevalim] in-Yisra'el. And-now, speak, please, to the-king, for he-will-not withhold-me from-you."

**13:14** And-not he-was-willing to-listen to-her-voice, and-he-was-stronger than-her, and-he-forced-her [vay'anneha] and-lay with-her.

**13:15** And-hated-her Amnon [with]-a-hatred very great, for greater [was] the-hatred that he-hated-her than the-love that he-had-loved-her. And-said to-her Amnon, "Arise, go!"

**13:16** And-she-said to-him, "No [al], because this evil [ra'ah], the-great, [is]-greater-than the-other that you-did with-me — to-send-me-away." And-not he-was-willing to-listen to-her.

**13:17** And-he-called his-servant, his-attendant [meshareto], and-said, "Send-out, please, this-one from-upon-me to-the-outside, and-bolt [ne'ol] the-door after-her."

**13:18** And-upon-her [was] a-robe of-long-sleeves [ketonet passim], for thus were-clothed [the]-daughters of-the-king, the-virgins [betulot], [in]-robes. And-brought-her-out his-attendant to-the-outside and-bolted the-door after-her.

**13:19** And-put Tamar ashes upon her-head, and-the-robe of-long-sleeves [ketonet ha-passim] that [was] upon-her she-tore, and-she-placed her-hand upon her-head and-went, walking and-crying-out [za'aqah].

**13:20** And-said to-her Avshalom her-brother, "Has Amnon your-brother been with-you? And-now, my-sister, be-silent [hacharishiy]; he [is] your-brother. Do-not set your-heart to this thing." And-sat Tamar, and-desolate [shomemah], in-[the]-house of-Avshalom her-brother.

**13:21** And-the-king David heard all these things, and-it-was-very-angry [vayichar] to-him.

**13:22** And-not spoke Avshalom with Amnon from-evil to good, for hated Avshalom Amnon on-[the]-word [al-devar] that he-forced Tamar his-sister.

**13:23** And-it-was to-two-years of-days [lishnatayim yamim], and-there-were shearers to-Avshalom in-Ba'al-Chatsor that [is] near Efrayim, and-invited Avshalom all [the]-sons of-the-king.

**13:24** And-came Avshalom to the-king and-said, "Behold, please, shearers [are] to-your-servant. Let-go, please, the-king and-his-servants with your-servant."

**13:25** And-said the-king to Avshalom, "No, my-son, let-us-not-go, all of-us, and-not let-us-be-heavy [nikbad] upon-you." And-he-pressed [vayifrats]-him, and-not he-was-willing to-go, and-he-blessed-him.

**13:26** And-said Avshalom, "And-if not, let-go, please, with-us Amnon my-brother." And-said to-him the-king, "Why should-he-go with-you?"

**13:27** And-pressed Avshalom upon-him, and-he-sent with-him Amnon and-all [the]-sons of-the-king.

**13:28** And-commanded Avshalom his-servants, saying, "See, please, when-is-good [the]-heart of-Amnon with-the-wine, and-I-say to-you, 'Strike Amnon!' — then-kill-him. Do-not fear. [Is]-it-not that I have-commanded-you? Be-strong and-be sons of-valor [benei-chayil]."

**13:29** And-did [the]-servants of-Avshalom to-Amnon as-that-which Avshalom had-commanded. And-rose-up all [the]-sons of-the-king, and-rode each upon his-mule [pirdo], and-fled.

**13:30** And-it-was — they [were] on the-way — and-the-report [shemu'ah] came to David, saying, "Struck Avshalom all [the]-sons of-the-king, and-not was-left of-them even one."

**13:31** And-rose-up the-king and-tore his-garments and-lay-down upon-the-ground, and-all his-servants [were]-standing [with]-garments torn.

**13:32** And-answered Yonadav son of-Shim'ah, brother of-David, and-said, "Let-not-say my-lord, all the-young-men, [the]-sons of-the-king, they-have-killed, for Amnon alone has-died, for upon [the]-mouth [al-piy] of-Avshalom it-was appointed [samah] from-the-day he-forced Tamar his-sister.

**13:33** And-now, let-not-place my-lord the-king upon his-heart the-thing, saying, 'All [the]-sons of-the-king have-died,' for only Amnon alone has-died."

**13:34** And-fled Avshalom. And-lifted-up the-youth, the-watchman [ha-tsofeh], his-eyes and-saw, and-behold, people many [were]-walking on the-road behind-him from-[the]-side of-the-mountain.

**13:35** And-said Yonadav to the-king, "Behold, [the]-sons of-the-king have-come; according-to-[the]-word of-your-servant, thus it-was."

**13:36** And-it-was as-he-finished to-speak, and-behold, [the]-sons of-the-king came, and-lifted-up their-voice and-wept. And-also the-king and-all his-servants wept [with]-a-weeping very great.

**13:37** And-Avshalom fled and-went to Talmai son of-Ammihud, king of-Geshur. And-he-mourned [vayit'abbel] over his-son all the-days.

**13:38** And-Avshalom fled and-went to-Geshur and-was there three years.

**13:39** And-longed [vatekhal] the-spirit [ruach] of-the-king David to-go-out to Avshalom, for he-was-comforted over Amnon, for he-had-died.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — vayetser lo:** Literally "and-it-was-narrow/constricted for-him." The verb *tsarar* denotes a pressing, squeezing anguish. The construction parallels the narrowness of Amnon's obsession — he is trapped by desire with no outlet, since Tamar is a *betulah* (virgin) under strict supervision.

**v.2 — yippale:** From the root פלא, "to be extraordinary/difficult/wonderful." Amnon finds it *impossible* (literally "beyond him") to do anything to her. The same root used for divine wonders is here used for the impossibility of acting on forbidden desire.

**v.5 — biryah:** The word for "food" here is related to *bar* (grain/health) — it is invalid/convalescent food, food for the sick. The entire ruse depends on the intimacy of hand-feeding.

**v.6 — levivot:** Heart-shaped cakes from the root *lev* (heart). The wordplay is deliberate: Amnon asks for "heart-cakes" while concealing his predatory intent. The verb *vattelabbev* (v.8) intensifies the wordplay — Tamar "heart-shaped" the cakes before his eyes.

**v.12 — al-te'anneniy:** The piel imperative of *'anah* — "to afflict, force, rape." Tamar uses the precise legal term for sexual violation. The same verb describes the affliction of Israel in Egypt (Exod 1:11-12).

**v.13 — nevalah:** "Outrage/disgrace/folly" — a term reserved for the most extreme violations of social and divine order. It appears in Gen 34:7 (Dinah's rape) and Judg 19:23-24 (the Levite's concubine). It marks the act as a rupture in the fabric of Israel.

**v.15 — the reversal:** The narrator's comment is devastating in its symmetry: *ki gedolah ha-sin'ah asher sene'ah meha-ahavah asher ahevah* — "for greater the hatred which he hated her than the love which he had loved her." The cognate accusative constructions mirror each other, revealing the obsession as its own opposite.

**v.18 — ketonet passim:** The same phrase used for Joseph's garment in Gen 37:3. The literary echo links two stories of sibling violence. Tamar, like Joseph, is a favored child whose special garment is destroyed by the violence of a brother.

**v.21 — LXX addition:** The Septuagint adds "but he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, for he loved him, because he was his firstborn" (cf. 4QSamᵃ). This reading explains David's inaction and is likely original, lost by haplography in the MT.

**v.37 — Talmai king of Geshur:** Absalom's maternal grandfather (cf. 2 Sam 3:3 — his mother was Maacah daughter of Talmai). His flight is to family, not random exile.

**v.39 — vatekhal:** The verb *kalah* can mean "to be finished/consumed/longing." The subject in the MT is ambiguous — some read "David" as subject (David longed to go out to Absalom), while others read the feminine verb form as indicating a feminine noun (*nefesh* or *ruach*) is understood. I supply *ruach* (spirit) following the implied syntax.

*— EMET*
